text:
[LGRA.8.5.10] A `where_clause` after a step's `within` belongs to that step,
in the one-line layout and the line-leading one alike, and sees every binding
before it as well as the step's own. A sequence has no sequence-wide `where`:
on a one-line sequence, a trailing `where` is the last step's. Nothing is lost,
because the last step's `where` already sees every binding of the sequence.
